title: American Golden Boot Race: The USMNT Stars With the Most Club Goals This Season
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Zach Lowy9:00 PM EDTCavan Sullivan (left), Julian Hall (center) and Sebastian Berhalter are dominating the domestic game. / Patrick Mulligan/USSF/Getty ImagesThe stars of the U.S. men’s national team are all too familiar with the back of the net.

American players across Major League Soccer have been scoring since February, given the 2026 season is now at its tail end, whereas those Americans overseas are only two months into the 2026–27 European season. Many of them have already opened their accounts, though, only adding to USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino’s selection headache for the upcoming international break.

Here, Sports Illustrated details all of the top American goal scorers of the various current club seasons, a running list that includes any player worldwide that has been rostered for the USMNT in the past 12 months and has scored at least one goal in their current club campaign. Although the MLS players have a significant head start on their teammates across the pond, it’s only a matter of time before those in Europe catch up.
Without further ado, let’s shed some light on the American Golden Boot race.

It wasn’t long ago that Folarin Balogun was the USMNT’s undisputed starting striker after an impressive World Cup showing. But with Balogun out of AS Monaco’s starting XI following a failed Premier League transfer, the path is clearing for Julian Hall to assert himself as Pochettino’s favored No. 9.

He only turned 18 years old in March, but Hall has already racked up 14 goals and four assists in 33 appearances this season for New York Red Bulls. He has relegated a Champions League veteran in Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting to the bench, while he continues to make history. Two years after becoming the second-youngest scorer in MLS history, Hall became the youngest player to score a hat trick in MLS, getting three past Columbus Crew back in May.

It’s no surprise that both the U.S. and Poland have set their sights on the teenage forward, with Hall making his USMNT debut in last month’s friendlies. After becoming the third player to score in each of his first three USMNT matches, all signs point to him becoming officially cap-tied during November’s Concacaf Nations League matches against Haiti.

When Ryan Richter took charge on May 27, Philadelphia Union had the worst record in MLS. But after a 15-match unbeaten run, which only came to an end last weekend against New England Revolution, the Union now sit sixth in the Eastern Conference. One of the most pivotal figures in Philly’s turnaround has been Cavan Sullivan.

Two years after becoming the youngest ever to play for a major North American professional sports team, Sullivan has confirmed the early hype with a breakout 2026 season. The winger has racked up 10 goals and 11 assists in 33 appearances, a record sum for an MLS teenager, and this month, he became the USMNT's youngest goalscorer after scoring in just his third cap against Mexico.

The 17-year-old is emerging as one of the best players in the whole continent. Enjoy him while you can, Philly fans. Sullivan is scheduled to join Manchester City in January 2028 after his 18th birthday.

New England Revolution haven’t played in a playoff match since 2023, and they haven’t won in the postseason since 2020. However, both droughts could be set to end this year, with the Revs currently sitting second in the Eastern Conference. A lot of the team’s newfound success can be credited to one youngster: Peyton Miller.

The 18-year-old winger has thrived for Marko Mitrović’s side, racking up seven goals and seven assists in 29 appearances. It remains to be seen whether his future is on the flanks or at the left back position, but Miller’s high-octane style and elite acceleration ensure that he has a resplendent future for club and country.

There are a few players who have scored five goals this club season, including Seattle Sounders captain Cristian Roldan and Real Salt Lake playmaker Diego Luna. Unlike Roldan, Luna was left off the World Cup roster and then was unable to return to the squad this fall after suffering a season-ending knee injury.
